name: Bhinda Sambhariya
subtitle: whole okra stuffed with a peanut, coconut and sesame masala, cooked gently in a covered pan

ingredients.qty: 3 tbsp, dry-roasted until it smells nutty

ingredients.note: use compounded-free hing to keep this gluten-free

prepNotes: Wash the okra a good hour ahead and dry each pod completely with a cloth. Any water left on them turns the whole dish slimy.
Roast the peanuts, sesame and besan separately and let them cool before grinding — warm nuts go pasty.
Choose small pods, 7-8cm; large okra is fibrous and splits when stuffed.

steps.text: Top and tail the okra and slit each pod lengthways down one side, stopping short of both ends so it stays whole.
Mix the ground peanut, roasted besan, sesame, coconut, all the ground spices, sugar, salt, ginger, chilli, coriander leaves and lemon juice into a crumbly stuffing.
steps.tip: It should just clump when squeezed. If it is dust-dry, add a teaspoon of oil, not water.

steps.text: Press the stuffing into each pod with a small spoon or your fingertip, filling but not splitting them.
Heat the oil in a wide kadhai, pop the mustard seeds and add the asafoetida.
Lay the stuffed okra in a single layer and let them sit undisturbed 4 minutes to blister on the underside.
steps.tip: Stirring early breaks the pods open and spills the masala.

steps.text: Turn each pod gently with tongs, cover, and cook on low heat 12 minutes.
Uncover, shake the pan and cook 5 minutes more until the okra is tender, the surfaces are lightly browned and no sliminess remains.
steps.tip: If it still looks ropey, finish uncovered on higher heat for 2 minutes — dry heat fixes it.

steps.text: Scatter over any leftover stuffing, let it toast for a minute, and serve with rotli.

storage: Keeps 2 days refrigerated. Reheat uncovered in a dry pan so the okra crisps again rather than steaming; the microwave makes it slippery.
